Many Harappans lived a peaceful, rural life.

The Madras Corporation is now called the.body: The Madras Corporation is now called the Greater Chennai Corporation. It was started on 29 September 1688. It is the oldest municipal body in India. One year earlier, the East India Company gave it a charter. The charter covered Fort St. George and nearby land. In 1792, Parliament passed an Act. The Act let it collect municipal taxes. Real municipal government began then.
The Madras Corporation is now called the.explanation: These facts show how the corporation grew, from its charter to real municipal government.
keyPoints: The Madras Corporation was started on 29 September 1688.
The East India Company gave the charter.
The 1792 Act let the corporation collect municipal taxes.

The Earth has a very, very long history,.title: Researchers of Earth's Past
The Earth has a very, very long history,.body: Earth has a very long history. Humans are only a tiny, recent part of it. Many people study this history. Geologists study soil, stones, hills, mountains and rivers. Palaeontologists study fossils. A fossil can be a footprint. It can also be a part of a plant or animal, kept for a long time. Anthropologists study how people live in groups, and their cultures. Archaeologists dig up remains from the past.
The Earth has a very, very long history,.explanation: Different researchers help us learn about Earth's long history.
keyPoints: Earth's history is very long. Humans are only a tiny, recent part.
Researchers study Earth's features, fossils, cultures and remains.
A fossil can be a footprint or a saved part of a plant or animal.

India has local, State, and Central gove.title: Three Levels of Government
India has local, State, and Central gove.body: India has local, State, and Central governments. Local authorities can deal with small floods. The State Government can send rescue teams. The Central Government can help with huge floods. Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha make national laws. The President is the nominal head of the Central executive. Nominal means head in name only. The Prime Minister is the executive head of the Central Government. The Governor is the nominal head of a State Government. The Chief Minister is the executive head of a State Government.
India has local, State, and Central gove.explanation: Each level of government has its own duties for floods and leadership.
keyPoints: Local authorities can deal with a small flood.
The State Government can send rescue teams.
The Central Government can help in a huge flood.

The tertiary sector is also called the s.title: Services in the Tertiary Sector
The tertiary sector is also called the s.body: The tertiary sector is also called the service sector. Technicians repair and service electronic items. These include mobile phones and televisions. Mechanics repair vehicles. These include cars and tractors. Electricians make sure electricity comes regularly. Mobile and internet services are part of this sector. Fruit and vegetable sellers sell farm crops to homes. Making software is a tertiary activity. So are services in hotels and restaurants.
The tertiary sector is also called the s.explanation: This sector has many useful services for homes and other places.
keyPoints: The tertiary sector is also called the service sector.
Technicians, mechanics and electricians give services.
Mobile, internet, hotel and restaurant services are tertiary activities.

Human living conditions improved in many.title: How communities grew
Human living conditions improved in many.body: Life got better for humans in many parts of the world. People settled down. They grew cereals and grains. They domesticated cattle and goats, which means they tamed them. More food helped communities grow in size and number. Communities often settled near rivers. Chieftains were in charge of community well-being, meaning health and happiness. The land was worked collectively. This means people worked together. Villages traded food, clothes and tools. New inventions included pottery and metals like copper and iron.
Human living conditions improved in many.explanation: These ideas show how farming and working together helped communities grow.
keyPoints: People settled down and grew cereals and grains.
More food helped communities grow.
People worked together and traded goods.

Panchayat Samitis help local people take.title: Local groups work together
Panchayat Samitis help local people take.body: Panchayat Samitis help local people take part in development. Their members differ between States. But their role stays the same. They collect plans from all Gram Panchayats. Then they combine the plans. They present these plans at district or State level. This helps get money for development projects. The Panchayat Samiti links the Gram Panchayat with the Zila Parishad. Special rules help disadvantaged groups make their needs heard.
Panchayat Samitis help local people take.explanation: Great start! These groups turn local plans into action for development.
keyPoints: Their role in helping local people take part stays the same.
Plans are combined and shown at district or State level.
One-third of seats are kept for women at all three levels.

People around us do different work. Geet.title: Work Around Us
People around us do different work. Geet.body: People around us have different jobs. Geeta Aunty is a pilot in the Indian Air Force. Kabir's grandfather left the Border Security Force. Now he takes care of a vegetable garden. He also does small jobs for his home. Anu's parents sell uniforms and ready-made clothes. Anu's mother teaches sewing in a volunteer group. Rohan is a software engineer. On weekends, he teaches computer skills. Free Geography classes are given to children nearby.
People around us do different work. Geet.explanation: This lesson shows many kinds of work around us.
keyPoints: People have different kinds of work.
Some people help their family and neighbours.
Some work is teaching and helping others.

India has defined borders, defined state.title: Looking at India's Past
India has defined borders, defined state.body: Today, India has clear borders, clear states and a known population. Long ago, it looked very different. The subcontinent means the land of India. It had many names. Its borders changed. We learn about India's past from old texts. We also use travellers' accounts, pilgrims' accounts and inscriptions. Inscriptions are written marks from the past. The Ṛig Veda is India's oldest text. It is several thousand years old.
India has defined borders, defined state.explanation: This lesson shows the sources we use to study India's past.
keyPoints: Long ago, India looked very different.
Old sources help us learn about India's past.
The Ṛig Veda is India's oldest text.

Aśhoka was an Indian emperor who lived a.title: Aśhoka and Bhārata
Aśhoka was an Indian emperor who lived a.body: Aśhoka was an emperor of India. He lived around 250 BCE. He left many inscriptions. His India had today's Bangladesh, Pakistan and parts of Afghanistan. A few centuries later, Bhārata became the common name for the Indian Subcontinent. The Viṣhṇu Purāṇa says Bhārata is north of the ocean. It is south of snowy mountains. Today, people write the name Bharat in northern India. In southern India, they write it Bharatam.
Aśhoka was an Indian emperor who lived a.explanation: This lesson links Aśhoka's empire with the ancient geography of Bhārata.
keyPoints: Aśhoka lived around 250 BCE and left many inscriptions.
Aśhoka's India included today's Bangladesh, Pakistan and parts of Afghanistan.
Bhārata became the common name for the Indian Subcontinent.

The Anthropological Survey of India is a.title: Studying India's Communities
The Anthropological Survey of India is a.body: The Anthropological Survey of India is a national group. It studied 4,635 communities in all States. It counted 325 languages. They are written in 25 scripts. India has over 1.4 billion people. This chapter says a migrant does not live near their birthplace or first community.
The Anthropological Survey of India is a.explanation: The survey counted India's languages. This chapter also explains the word 'migrant'.
keyPoints: The survey studied communities in all States.
It counted languages and their scripts.
A migrant does not live near their birthplace or first community.

Farmers around Anand sold milk to a near.title: Farmers Build Together
Farmers around Anand sold milk to a near.body: Farmers near Anand sold milk to a dairy nearby. The farmers went to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel together. Patel told them to form a cooperative. He also told them to be independent. A cooperative means farmers work together as a group. Independent means they do not need middlemen, or people in between. The group collected milk, processed it and sent it out. They built a factory in Anand. AMUL started in 1946 CE. Sharing work helped their income grow slowly.
Farmers around Anand sold milk to a near.explanation: Working together helped farmers slowly raise their income.
keyPoints: A cooperative is farmers working together as a group.
AMUL started in 1946 CE.
Sharing work helped farmers raise their income slowly.

Buddhism was a school of thought, meanin.title: Gautama's Search
Buddhism was a school of thought, meanin.body: Buddhism is a school of thought. It is a set of shared ideas. It did not accept Vedic authority. Siddhārtha Gautama was born a prince in Lumbini. At 29, he saw an old person, a sick person and a dead body. He left the palace. He searched for the cause of human suffering. He sat under a pipal tree and meditated. He gained enlightenment. Enlightenment means deep understanding. He taught that ignorance and attachment cause suffering.
Buddhism was a school of thought, meanin.explanation: These ideas came from Gautama's search for the cause of suffering.
keyPoints: Gautama left the palace to search for the cause of suffering.
Ignorance and attachment cause suffering.
Ahimsa means not hurting or injuring.

Halma is a tradition that brings people.title: Helping the Community
Halma is a tradition that brings people.body: Halma is a tradition. It brings people together. Its main aim is to serve Mother Earth. The Bhils dug trenches to save rainwater. They did this work without pay. It was their duty to help the community and the environment. Other groups cooked food. They gave the food to people in need. Kamal Parmar taught children every evening. Kamal Parmar gave them dinner. Later, older students helped as volunteers.
Halma is a tradition that brings people.explanation: These actions show people helping communities, the environment and children.
keyPoints: Halma brings people together to help anyone in trouble.
The Bhils saved rainwater through community service.
Kamal Parmar helped children by teaching them and giving free meals.

Panchayati Raj lets villagers take an ac.title: Local Participation and Village Administration
Panchayati Raj lets villagers take an ac.body: Panchayati Raj lets villagers take part. It includes developing villages and local areas. Its work is a little different in each State. States have authority over it. The Arthaśhāstra is an old text about governance. Kauṭilya wrote it about 2,300 years ago. Sangrahaṇa, kārvaṭika, droṇamukha and sthānīya were four types of village administration. Panchayati Raj is a democracy. It uses direct participation and elected representatives.
Panchayati Raj lets villagers take an ac.explanation: These ideas link local participation, State authority and old administration.
keyPoints: Villagers take part in local development.
States have authority over Panchayati Raj institutions.
The Arthaśhāstra lists four types of village administration.

Urban local bodies have different highes.title: Urban local bodies
Urban local bodies have different highes.body: Cities have different local bodies. Cities above 10 lakhs have a Municipal Corporation. It is called a Mahanagar Nigam. Cities with 1 to 10 lakhs have a Municipal Council. It is called a Nagar Palika. Small towns and cities have a Nagar Panchayat. Indore Municipal Corporation gives services. These include property tax, water charges and solid waste management. Citizen services include certificates, fire services and licences. It also gives water tankers and debris clearance.
Urban local bodies have different highes.explanation: This card tells about each big local body. It also tells about some Indore services.
keyPoints: Municipal Corporations serve cities above 10 lakhs.
Municipal Councils serve cities with 1 to 10 lakhs.
Nagar Panchayats serve smaller cities and towns.

People work together to keep their surro.title: Working Together for a Clean India
People work together to keep their surro.body: People work together to keep their area clean. Swachh Bharat Abhiyan needs all Indian citizens to work together. People also clean their homes. Everyone does their own part. People clean streets, roads, parks and other public places. Together, they can keep the home, neighbourhood, society and nation clean. Van Mahotsav brings people together to plant trees. It also teaches why trees matter.
People work together to keep their surro.explanation: When people work together, they make communities cleaner.
keyPoints: Every citizen helps keep the area clean.
People clean shared places together.
Van Mahotsav helps people plant trees.

History has many sources. A source can b.title: Clues About the Past
History has many sources. A source can b.body: History has many sources. A source is a place, person, text or object. It tells us about the past. Every object or structure can tell a story about the past. We can learn family history from photos, diaries, ID cards and memories. Historians collect many sources. They check where the sources agree. Some pieces of history may still be missing.
History has many sources. A source can b.explanation: Historians use different clues to learn about the past.
keyPoints: Sources can be places, people, texts or objects.
Objects and structures can tell stories about the past.
Historians collect and check many sources.

Tenzing’s family shares many responsibil.title: A Family That Helps Together
Tenzing’s family shares many responsibil.body: Tenzing’s family shares many jobs. His father runs a small grocery shop. He also helps with housework. His mother works at a local handicraft cooperative (a group that makes crafts). Now she is often busy. When she is busy, his father helps clean the house. His grandmother tells fun stories. They are funny and wise. His grandfather helps with homework. He also does social work (helps people) in the colony. The family talks about big costs. They save money for surprise needs.
Tenzing’s family shares many responsibil.explanation: Tenzing’s family shows that everyone can share jobs.
keyPoints: Family members share work at home and in the colony.
Grandparents help with homework, stories and social work.
The family plans costs and saves for surprise needs.

Urban local bodies are the local governm.title: How urban local bodies work
Urban local bodies are the local governm.body: Urban local bodies are local governments in cities and towns. They are decentralised. This means decisions are made near local people. Local people have a direct say. They help run their areas. Cities and towns are divided into smaller areas. These areas are called wards. Ward committees plan activities. They watch for problems. They report problems to the authorities. The way wards work is different in each State.
Urban local bodies are the local governm.explanation: This card explains wards and how problems are reported.
keyPoints: Urban local bodies are decentralised local governments.
Local people have a direct say in running their areas.
Wards are small areas inside cities and towns.
Ward committees plan activities and report problems to authorities.

**Longitude** tells you how far a place.title: East and west
**Longitude** tells you how far a place.body:
**Longitude** tells how far a place is from the Prime Meridian. You measure it east or west along the Equator.

It goes from **0°** to **180°**. We add **E** for east. We add **W** for west. (180° has no letter.)

Delhi is 77°E. Tokyo is 140°E. New York is 74°W.
**Longitude** tells you how far a place.explanation: E means east of the Prime Meridian. W means west of it.
keyPoints: Longitude: how far from the Prime Meridian.
0° to 180°, with E or W.

People have lived in communities for a v.title: How rules help us live together
People have lived in communities for a v.body: People have lived in communities for a very long time. Living together can cause arguments and disorder. Society could not work if nobody followed rules. Families, schools, exams and roads all have rules. Governance means making decisions and organising society. It also makes sure rules are followed. A government makes rules. It makes sure people follow them. Laws are very important rules. Rules and laws can change. Citizens, the people of a country, can have a say about them.
People have lived in communities for a v.explanation: Rules help people live together. Governance helps rules work.
keyPoints: Communities need rules to work.
Governance organises society. It makes sure rules are followed.
Citizens can have a say about laws and rules.

Irrigation has increased farm production.title: Good Things and Problems
Irrigation has increased farm production.body: Irrigation means bringing water to farms. It helps farms grow more food. But irrigation also lowers groundwater. Groundwater is water under the ground. River life includes farming and fishing. Rivers on plains are easy to travel on. The land slopes down gently. Many communities hold festivals and ceremonies at holy river places. These facts show how river plains help work, travel and community life.
Irrigation has increased farm production.explanation: This shows the good and bad of irrigation.
keyPoints: Irrigation helps farms grow more food.
Irrigation also lowers groundwater.
Holy river places are used for community events.

The Mahābhārata is one of India's most f.title: Old Names for Parts of India
The Mahābhārata is one of India's most f.body: The Mahābhārata is one of India's most famous old books. It lists many regional names. A regional name is an old name for a part of India. Kāshmīra is about today's Kashmir. Kurukṣhetra is in today's Haryana. Vanga is in Bengal. Prāgjyotiṣha is about today's Assam. Kaccha is today's Kutch. The name Kerala was used for about today's Kerala.
The Mahābhārata is one of India's most f.explanation: These old names help us link the book to places in India.
keyPoints: The Mahābhārata lists many places.
Old writings used names for different parts of India.
These names help us link the book to places today.

The name Bharata first appears in the Ṛi.title: How the Name Bharata Changed
The name Bharata first appears in the Ṛi.body: The name Bharata first appears in the Ṛig Veda. There, Bharata is the name of one main Vedic group. Later writings mention some kings named Bharata. In the Mahābhārata, Bhāratavarṣa is a wider name. It is the name for the whole Indian Subcontinent. The book names many rivers and groups of people under this wider name.
The name Bharata first appears in the Ṛi.explanation: The word Bharata has different meanings in different writings.
keyPoints: Bharata first appears in the Ṛig Veda.
At first, it names a main Vedic group of people.
Bhāratavarṣa has a wider meaning in the Mahābhārata.

The Upanishads built on Vedic ideas and.title: Ideas from the Upanishads
The Upanishads built on Vedic ideas and.body: The Upanishads built on Vedic ideas. They added new ideas. They taught about rebirth and karma. Rebirth means being born again after death. Brahman is the divine essence. Ātman means the Self. Ātman is in every living being. The Upanishads teach that everything is connected. One prayer asks for happiness for all creatures. Some schools grew from the Vedas. They became the base of Hinduism. Yoga developed ways to truly know brahman in the mind.
The Upanishads built on Vedic ideas and.explanation: These ideas show what the Upanishads thought about life and the Self.
keyPoints: The Upanishads taught about rebirth and karma.
Brahman is the divine essence. Ātman is the Self.
Yoga developed ways to truly know brahman.

Families are the oldest and most basic u.title: Different Family Types
Families are the oldest and most basic u.body: Families are the oldest and most basic group in society. Almost everyone lives in a family. A joint family has several generations living together. Generations means grandparents, parents and children. A nuclear family is mostly two parents and their children. Sometimes, a nuclear family has one parent and children. Family ties create strong bonds between all the children.
Families are the oldest and most basic u.explanation: This card shows family types and how family members are connected.
keyPoints: A joint family has several generations living together.
A nuclear family is mostly two parents and their children.
Family ties create strong bonds between all the children.

To measure longitude, we need a starting.title: The Prime Meridian
To measure longitude, we need a starting.body:
To measure longitude, we need a starting line. It is called the **Prime Meridian**.

In **1884**, some countries agreed to use the meridian through **Greenwich**. Greenwich is in London, England. This line is marked **0°** longitude.
To measure longitude, we need a starting.explanation: Counting longitude starts at Greenwich, in London.
keyPoints: The Prime Meridian is the starting line for longitude.
It passes through Greenwich, in London.
It is 0°.

Latitude and longitude are the two **coo.title: Latitude and longitude together
Latitude and longitude are the two **coo.body:
Latitude and longitude are the two **coordinates** of a place. Together, they can find any place on Earth!

“Delhi lies at about **29°N** latitude and **77°E** longitude.”

All these lines make a **grid**.

The Equator divides Earth into the **Northern** and **Southern** Hemispheres. The Prime Meridian divides it into the **Western** and **Eastern** Hemispheres.
Latitude and longitude are the two **coo.explanation: Latitude and longitude are the two coordinates we use to find a place.
keyPoints: Latitude + longitude = coordinates.
The Equator: Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
The Prime Meridian: Western and Eastern Hemispheres.

Standard times are grouped into **time z.title: Time zones
Standard times are grouped into **time z.body:
Standard times are grouped into **time zones**. The lines between zones are **not perfectly straight**. They **tend to follow** country borders.

Some big countries need more than one time zone. The **USA has six** time zones. **Russia has 11**.
Standard times are grouped into **time z.explanation: Some big countries need more than one time zone.
keyPoints: Time zone lines tend to follow country borders.
The USA has six time zones. Russia has 11.

Oceans have smaller extensions, such as.title: Saltwater and freshwater
Oceans have smaller extensions, such as.body: Oceans have smaller parts, such as seas, bays and gulfs. Most of Earth's water is in the oceans. Seawater is salty and not safe for most land animals, including humans. Freshwater is only a very small part of Earth's water. It is found in glaciers, rivers, lakes, the air and underground. Water underground is called **groundwater**.
Oceans have smaller extensions, such as.explanation: Most water is salty. Only a small part is freshwater.
keyPoints: Oceans contain most of Earth's water.
Seawater is salty and not safe for most land animals.
Freshwater is a very small part of Earth's water.

Plains are extensive flat or gently undu.title: Life on the Plains
Plains are extensive flat or gently undu.body: Plains are big, flat lands. Some plains are gently rolling. They are usually no more than 300 metres above sea level. Rivers leave **sediments** (mud and soil) on them. This makes the soil **fertile**, good for growing crops. The first civilisations grew up near rivers on these plains. Many people live there. Farming, river fishing, easy river travel and holy festivals are important parts of river life.
Plains are extensive flat or gently undu.explanation: Plains have rich soil, calm rivers and lively communities.
keyPoints: Plains are flat or gently rolling.
Plains are usually no more than 300 metres above sea level.
River sediments make plains fertile.

The Harappan civilisation was India's ea.title: The Harappan Civilisation
The Harappan civilisation was India's ea.body: The Harappan civilisation was India's earliest civilisation. It has several names. Some are Harappan, Indus and Indus-Sarasvatī Civilisation. Its people were called Harappans. Harappa, in Sindh, was the first city excavated (dug up). Important cities grew along rivers, including Mohenjo-daro and Harappa.
The Harappan civilisation was India's ea.explanation: Now you know its names, its people and its important cities.
keyPoints: The Harappan civilisation was India's earliest civilisation.
Its people were called Harappans.
Harappa was the first city excavated (dug up).

Harappans valued water management, which.title: How Harappans Managed Water
Harappans valued water management, which.body: Harappans cared a lot about **water management**. This means caring for water and using it properly. They also cared about cleanliness. Many homes had their own bathing areas. These joined bigger drains under the streets. The drains carried waste water away. Mohenjo-daro had hundreds of wells made of bricks. In other places, people may have taken water from ponds, streams or **reservoirs** (large water tanks). Dholavira had at least six large reservoirs. Most were joined by underground drains.
Harappans valued water management, which.explanation: These facts show how well Harappans looked after water.
keyPoints: Harappans cared about water management and cleanliness.
Home bathing areas joined bigger drains.
Mohenjo-daro had hundreds of wells made of bricks.
Most reservoirs at Dholavira were joined by underground drains.

India has an immense variety of festival.title: Festivals Across India
India has an immense variety of festival.body: India has many kinds of festivals. Some festivals are celebrated all over India. Common festivals often happen at about the same time. Similar festivals can have different names in different places. Makara Sankrānti starts the harvest season (the time when crops are cut) in many parts of India. It is celebrated on or around January 14. Many big festivals happen in October and November.
India has an immense variety of festival.explanation: Festivals bring different places together. This is true even if names or dates are different.
keyPoints: India has many different festivals.
Some festivals are celebrated all over India.
Similar festivals can have different names.
Makara Sankrānti starts the harvest season in many parts.

Digital technology gives criminals new w.title: How the Three Branches Work Together
Digital technology gives criminals new w.body: Digital tools give criminals new ways to steal money. Cybercrime means crime done with digital tools. Governments have made new laws to fight cybercrime. The legislature is a group of representatives (people who speak for others). It makes and updates laws. The executive puts these laws into action. The judiciary uses courts to decide if someone broke a law. These three branches of government work together.
Digital technology gives criminals new w.explanation: Different jobs help the government handle cybercrime.
keyPoints: Crime done with digital tools is cybercrime.
New laws can fight cybercrime.
Each branch has a different job.
Three branches work together.

Democracy is a foundation stone of the g.title: What is democracy?
Democracy is a foundation stone of the g.body: Democracy is the base of how most countries are governed. The word democracy comes from two Greek words. Kratos means rule or power. Democracy means rule of the people. India is a representative democracy. At state level and national level, people vote for representatives. MLAs represent people at state level. MPs represent people at national level.
Democracy is a foundation stone of the g.explanation: Democracy lets people choose representatives by voting.
keyPoints: Democracy means rule of the people.
India is a representative democracy.
MLAs and MPs represent people at different levels.

India is very large and varied. About tw.title: Local government in rural India
India is very large and varied. About tw.body: India is very big. It has many kinds of people and places. About two-thirds of India's people live in rural areas. A Panchayat is a village council (a group that makes village decisions). Panchayati Raj means self-government. Local people run it. It brings government closer to villages. Local people can join decisions. They can solve local problems. They can help development (making life better) grow. The system has three levels. Its work includes agriculture (farming), housing, roads and water resources (water for people).
India is very large and varied. About tw.explanation: These ideas help you understand local government in rural India.
keyPoints: A Panchayat is a village council.
Panchayati Raj is self-government by local people.
It has three levels. It covers local development work.

**Latitude** tells you how far a place i.title: Latitude
**Latitude** tells you how far a place i.body:
**Latitude** tells you how far a place is from the Equator.

Stand on the Equator. Then walk towards a pole. At any point, draw an imaginary line (not a real line) from east to west. It is parallel to the Equator. It is a **parallel of latitude**. It makes a circle around the Earth.
**Latitude** tells you how far a place i.explanation: Latitude is about north and south of the Equator.
keyPoints: Latitude is how far a place is from the Equator.
A parallel of latitude runs east to west.

Opposite the Prime Meridian is the **Int.title: The International Date Line
Opposite the Prime Meridian is the **Int.body:
The **International Date Line** is opposite the **Prime Meridian**. It is at about **180°** longitude.

If you cross it going **east**, you **subtract** (take away) **a day**. For example, it changes from Monday to Sunday.

If you cross it going **west**, you **add a day** (one more day). For example, it changes from Sunday to Monday.
Opposite the Prime Meridian is the **Int.explanation: East subtracts a day. West adds a day.
keyPoints: The Date Line is at about 180°.
East: subtract a day.
West: add a day.

White shapes from space are cloud masses.title: Rain, storms and tsunamis
White shapes from space are cloud masses.body: From space, clouds look white. Clouds bring rain to the land. India's monsoon rains start over the ocean. Oceans make cyclones. Cyclones can damage places near the coast. Earthquakes or volcanoes cause tsunamis. Tsunamis start at the bottom of the ocean. Tsunamis are huge waves. They travel thousands of kilometres. They flood areas near the coast. We can often find tsunamis before they reach the coast. Disaster management helps when people lose life or homes.
White shapes from space are cloud masses.explanation: This card joins rain, storms, tsunamis and disaster management.
keyPoints: Clouds bring rain to the land.
Cyclones can damage places near the coast.
Tsunamis are huge, powerful waves.

The Viṣhṇu Purāṇa is an ancient text tha.title: How Bhārata Was Described
The Viṣhṇu Purāṇa is an ancient text tha.body: The Viṣhṇu Purāṇa is an old text. It describes Bhārata. People called Bhārata the land north of the ocean. It was also called the land south of the snowy mountains. Some centuries after Aśhoka, Bhārata became the general name for the Indian Subcontinent. People still use this name today.
The Viṣhṇu Purāṇa is an ancient text tha.explanation: Old writers described Bhārata by its place on the Subcontinent.
keyPoints: The Viṣhṇu Purāṇa is an old text about Bhārata.
Bhārata was north of the ocean and south of snowy mountains.
People still use the name Bhārata today.

Ancient Chinese people interacted with I.title: Journeys and names
Ancient Chinese people interacted with I.body: Ancient Chinese people had contact with India. Xuanzang travelled there in the 7th century CE. He visited many places. He met scholars. He collected Buddhist texts. After 17 years, he went back to China. He translated Sanskrit manuscripts. Other Chinese scholars also visited India over many centuries. Tianzhu came from Sindhu. It could mean heavenly master. Hindustān first appeared in a Persian inscription about 1,800 years ago. Later, most invaders used this name for the Subcontinent.

keyPoints: Xuanzang travelled to India and collected Buddhist texts.
